perks.name: Cooling Baubles
perks.desc:
Collecting an Elemental pickup, collecting an Orb of Power, or destroying a Tangle reduces heat.

Elemental pickups include [Solar]Firesprites, [Void]Void Breaches, [Arc]Ionic Traces, [Stasis]Stasis Shards, and [Strand]Strand Tangles.

perks.name: Eddy Current
perks.desc: Temporarily increases reload speed and handling after sprinting or while amplified. This effect is improved when you are amplified.

perks.name: Hip-Fire Grip
perks.desc: Increases accuracy, stability, and precision hit targeting when firing from the hip.

perks.name: Attrition Orbs
perks.desc: Dealing sustained damage creates an Orb of Power.

perks.name: Trickle Charge
perks.desc: Receiving or discharging Bolt Charge partially loads the magazine from reserves.

perks.name: Gutshot Straight
perks.desc: Aiming down sights increases body shot damage, decreases target acquisition.

perks.name: Delicate Tuning
perks.desc: While at low heat, this weapon has improved range, handling, and accuracy.

perks.name: Jolting Feedback
perks.desc:
Dealing repeated damage with this weapon inflicts Jolt. 

While amplified, Jolt is applied faster.

perks.name: One for All
perks.desc: Hitting three separate targets increases damage for a moderate duration.

perks.name: Rolling Storm
perks.desc:
Final blows grant Bolt Charge.
While amplified, final blows grant additional Bolt Charge.

perks.name: Frenzy
perks.desc: Being in combat for an extended time increases damage, handling, and reload for this weapon until you are out of combat.

perks.name: Offhand Strike
perks.desc: Final blows grant additional weapon range, stability, and accuracy when firing from the hip for a short duration.

perks.name: Killing Tally
perks.desc: Kills increase this weapon's damage until it is stowed or reloaded.

perks.name: Thermal Atomization
perks.desc: While at high heat, this weapon deals increased damage and causes targets to explode when defeated.

perks.name: Imperial Allegiance
perks.desc: Being near allies grants increased cooling or charge rate, and increased damage while at high heat or low guard energy.

notes: Constructed by @Adamsdown_Boy (PvE PvE-Boss PvE-SustainedDamage PvE-EndGame PvE-God M+KB Controller): First-choice PvE roll for sustained DPS against a single yellow-bar target in activities rated Normal, Hard or Very Hard difficulty, particularly with Arc builds. Bitter End is a Balanced Heat frame LMG, with a rapid-fire firing rate which are rated C-Tier for endgame PvE by @TheAegisRelic Endgame Analysis Spreadsheet​, who says "good damage profile but mediocre total damage and worst recoil of any LMG frame". The heat frame offers built in Anti-Overload, and is like an extra perk set, first providing reduced heat generation, significantly increasing the number of shots before overheating, and providing a pseudo-Reconstruction, slowly "refilling" as the weapon loses heat when not being used. Additionally, there's an intrinsic ×1.15 damage boost against orange and yellow bars and vehicles, plus a ×2 vent rate if you manually reload when the heat bar is at >87.5% of maximum heat to proc Perfect Vent, as per the Destiny Data Compendium. The recoil direction is just left of vertical and pretty tight so you could improve recoil control or look to boost Stability to help hit crits with the barrel perk, or just boost Handling if you can land your shots. In the heatsink perk slot, perks that reduce Heat Generation or Vent Speed work best for this roll. Bitter End can be used for boss damage, particularly for Arc builds. If you're behind a Storm's Keep rally barricade, Trickle Charge reduces 10% heat on receiving a stack of Arc Bolt Charge, and 20% when you discharge with a lightning bolt on a target. Otherwise, if someone on your fireteam is producing power orbs, or you can generate Ionic Traces, Cooling Baubles reduces weapon heat by 33% for each Elemental pickup or power orb collected. In the second column for both target and AoE damage, Jolting Feedback applies Arc Jolt after 14 hits (11 when amplified) to tougher enemies who can survive the weapon damage, triggering chain lightning on further hits, or Rolling Storm generates ×2 stacks of Arc Bolt Charge on a kill, to trigger a lightning bolt at ×10 stacks. Aegis ranks the Imperial Allegiance origin trait as A-Tier - used in a fireteam, it stacks up to ×3 per ally within 15m, boosting cooling by a max ×1.105 and increasing damage when above 50% heat by max ×1.105. If you're interested, this is modelled on on the Z-6 rotary blaster cannon used by Hevy in the Clone Wars series. The name "bitter end" comes from old sailing ship terminology. The "bitts" are the heavy wooden or iron posts on the deck used to secure cables and ropes. The very last section of an anchor rope attached to the bitts is called the "bitter end." So, when an anchor rope was let out all the way to its absolute limit, a sailor reached the bitter end - meaning there was no rope left to give. It's also thought by the community to be a subtle linguistic joke: you start with "Sweet Business," and you finish with the "Bitter End". Recommended MW: Handling, with your preferred choice of mod to boost weapon stats, ammo generation, or elemental pickups for builds.

Inspired by @CourtProjects, @Saint_Kabr and and @ImpetusAlways (PvE PvE-MajorSpec PvE-EndGame PvE-God M+KB Controller): First-choice PvE roll for burst damage against Banes, Elites, Champions and Minibosses in both general at-level or better, and end-game underleveled content, particularly for arc builds. Bitter End is a Balanced Heat frame LMG, with a rapid-fire firing rate, which are rated D-Tier for endgame PvE by @TheAegisRelic tiering spreadsheet https://linktr.ee/TheAegisRelic for having significantly worse base total damage than other LMGs due to total ammo reserves of only 433. The heat frame is like an extra perk set, first providing reduced heat generation, significantly increasing the number of shots before overheating, and providing a pseudo-Reconstruction, automatically "refilling" as the weapon loses heat when not being used. Additionally, there's an intrinsic ×1.15 damage boost against orange and yellow bars and vehicles, plus a ×2 vent rate if you manually reload when the heat bar is at >87.5% of maximum heat to proc Perfect Vent, as per the https://www.destiny2.science/ Destiny Data Compendium. The stats are weird by comparison with other rapid-fire LMGs - see https://d2foundry.gg/w/954563454 for how the weapon stats impact in-game performance, once the formulas have been worked out. With the high base stability you should be able to control the recoil and focus on Handling with the barrel perk. For the heatsink perk, look for something that reduces heat generation, or improves cooling efficiency or vent speed. To pair with the arc toolkit, in the first trait perk column you could look for Trickle Charge to refill 10% of the magazine on receiving a stack of Bolt Charge, and 20% when you discharge with a lightning bolt on a target, or use Ionic Traces to proc Cooling Baubles which reduces weapon heat by 33% for each Elemental pickup or power orb collected. Alternatively, there's Attrition Orbs to spawn a power orb after 45-50 hits within 5s of each other (so that's an orb every 3-4s) to proc armour mods. For additional damage against tougher enemies, Jolting Feedback - applies Jolt after 16 hits (14 when enhanced and 11 when amplified) to tougher enemies who can survive the weapon damage, triggering chain lightning on further hits for both target and AoE damage. If there are adds nearby, you could also use Killing Tally which gains a stack for each enemy killed up to ×3 to boost damage by up to ×1.3 until you reload or stow, or One For All which boosts damage by ×1.35 for a non-refreshable 10s (11s when enhanced) after hitting three separate targets within 3s of each. The Origin Trait, Imperial Allegiance grants a stack for each ally in 15m, up to ×3, to boost both the cooling rate and damage when heat is >50% by up to a max of ×1.105, so is ideal for working in a fireteam. If you're interested, this is modelled on on the Z-6 rotary blaster cannon used by Hevy in the Clone Wars series. Recommended MW: Cooling Efficiency, with a Heat Generated mod or your preferred choice of mod to boost weapon stats, ammo generation, or elemental pickups for builds - and don't forget to check any available seasonal fragile mods.

Inspired by https://www.youtube.com/@cammycakesgaming (PvP PvP-KillChain PvP-God M+KB Controller): God-roll PvP for kill-chaining. Bitter End is, right now, an S-Tier heavy weapon option - at the time of writing you'll pick up 75 shots from a brick which is enough for 10 kills, which feels like a mistake so expect that to be nerfed. It's a Heat weapon - which means you get an ersatz Reconstruction for free from the passive cooling - with a rapid-fire fire rate. The Balanced Heat frame provides a ×2 vent rate if you manually vent when weapon heat is >87.5%. The @hugowo_ spreadsheet at https://www.destiny2.science/, shows the TTK at base as 0.400s (7c0b) - increasing the weapons stat doesn't reduce this, but at 142 does mean you'll need less crits (6c1b). The 80% crit accuracy-adjusted TTK is 0.467s (4c4b), which becomes is easier at a 122 weapon stat (3c5b) and then 194 (2c6b). The stats are decent compared to other rapid fire LMGs - higher Range, Stability and Recoil Direction but lower Handling. You can see the in-game effect of stat changes at https://d2foundry.gg/w/954563454 for yourself, once the formulas have been worked out. For the barrel perk, you could go either Handling, or Range if you're using Shrewd Survivor armour for the two-piece Reflex Action set bonus to boost Handling and Accuracy. For the Battery Perk, Ionized Heatsink reduces heat generation, and the manual vent penalty isn't so much of problem with the passive cooling. For kill-chaining, the double damage trait perk pair of Gutshot Straight grants ×1.1 bodyshot damage when ADSed at the price of ×0.8 sized aim assist cone size - which means you can hit the 0.467s TTK with no crits needed (0c8b), and Killing Tally for an escalating boost to damage of up to ×1.3 damage after three kills - just one stack reduces the TTK to 0.400s (2c5b) and two or three stacks means you need no crits again (0c7b). The Imperial Allegiance origin trait is situationally useful if you're near one, two or three teammates when heat is >50%, boosting both cooling efficiency and damage by up to ×1.105, but Accelerated Assault is probably better, proccing 10% cooling and ×1.05 damage when you hit 3 times with 1.2-4s between each hit. Recommended MW: Handling or Cooling Efficiency, with a Heat Generated mod/enhanced mod, or your choice depending on your play style.
